about: What a .tidegraph holds (notes/visual-scripting.md): every kind of declaration, member and node, the keys of each in the order tidec writes them, and a node's ports. tidec reads it for its own nodes' inputs; tidels serves it to graph editors (tide/graphSchema).

rules: An input takes one wire; wiring another replaces it.
A statement runs from one place: an exec output takes one wire, and a statement is wired from one exec output.
No value is made of itself: a data wire can't close a loop.
A value wired to two inputs is worked out at each.
A local is read where what declares it has run.
A simple value is in the input that reads it: a number, text, a name, a path of fields. A value worked out by a call or an operator is a node wired in.

inline.about: What never changes is in the input that reads it, typed or picked there, and is no node of its own, as a Blueprint pin's default: a literal (always), a name in PascalCase or FULL_CASE, so a type, a namespace, an enum or a constant (named), a member of what is itself shown there (path: Math.PI, Phase.Running, Color.red), a '-' over a number (negative), a vector or a colour made of numbers alone (numbers: a call named one of numbersOf whose arguments are all numbers, float2(16, 14)). Each is read by one input. A variable (a parameter, a local, a field) is a Get node, which can be wired to any number of inputs. What a Set or a step changes (its target), a name, a local or a member read by it alone, is in its title (titled: Set score; Set speed; Set scale, its Target wired in). tidec's layout gives what's shown in an input no room (graph_layout_fold).

look.about: How the graph editors draw, the same in each: every colour (dark and light; a host only says which), every size in pixels at zoom 1, and the font, which each editor ships. headers: a node's title bar by its category's name, and the entry's. types: a pin's and a wire's colour by its value's type; a type not listed gets a hue of its name (h = h * 31 + each UTF-16 unit, unsigned 32-bit, hue h mod 360, with typeHue's saturation and lightness). A wire with no type known takes its source node's category colour. Where the rows of one box have the same parts (a card's members, an entry's parameters, a node's inputs and its own fields, My game's list, Details' lines), each part is a column, left-aligned, as wide as its widest cell in that box: a cell with something in it starts columnGap after the end of the column before it, and a column empty in every row takes no room.
